about.body1: Tap any term — get a context-aware translation that knows the book's domain. Tap «attention» in an ML chapter and you get «увага (механізм у нейромережах)» in Ukrainian, not the everyday meaning. Words you save feed a capped weekly SRS queue with multiple-choice cards generated by a local Gemma 4 model running on a $20 VPS — no per-user cloud costs.
about.creator.bio1: I built TextStack because I quit Designing Data-Intensive Applications three times before this. Not because the book was hard — I understood most of what was on the page — but because forty unfamiliar terms broke my flow. Summarizing it away defeated the point. So I built the thing I wanted: tap a term, get the context, keep reading.
about.creator.bio2: It's an open project I run because I needed it. AGPL-3.0, full codebase on GitHub. If you share the use case or want to contribute, I'd love to hear from you.
about.creator.heading: The Creator
about.intro: TextStack is an open-source reader for developers who want to finish dense English technical books in their native language.
about.mission1: Real understanding of a technical book comes from finishing it — not from skipping unfamiliar terms or summarizing it away. TextStack is built around that: keep the book in front of you, let the friction (vocabulary, terminology, domain) get out of the way.
about.mission2: Every feature — domain-aware translation, vocabulary builder, spaced repetition, reading stats — exists for one job: get you to the last page of the kind of book you usually quit halfway through.
about.openSource1: TextStack is licensed under GNU AGPL-3.0. The full codebase — .NET 10 backend, React frontend, React Native mobile app — lives at github.com/mrviduus/textstack. You can self-host the entire stack on a $20/month consumer VPS, no GPU required.
about.seoDesc: Open-source reader for developers who want to finish dense English technical books in their native language. Local LLM, AGPL-3.0, self-hostable on a $20 VPS.
about.seoTitle: About TextStack — open-source reader for developers
about.tech1: Local Gemma 4 model (via Ollama) generates the multiple-choice distractors, vocabulary hints, and book metadata enrichment on your own server — no per-user cloud LLM costs. OpenAI's gpt-4.1-mini handles the translation layer where multilingual quality matters.
about.techStackValue: ASP.NET Core 10 · PostgreSQL 16 · React 19 · React Native (Expo) · Ollama (Gemma 4) · OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini · Docker · Cloudflare Tunnel

deleteAccount.retentionBody: Deletion happens immediately, in a single transaction — there is no waiting period and no recovery window. A few copies outlive it for a limited time and then expire on their own: encrypted backups (up to about 90 days), cached translations, explanations and speech (30 days), web server request logs (14 days), application logs (overwritten by size, typically within weeks) and crash reports (Sentry's retention period). Include your contact details, identify the removed material, state under penalty of perjury that the removal was a mistake or misidentification, and consent to the jurisdiction of a US federal court (or, if outside the US, your local equivalent).
dmca.howBody: To file a valid takedown notice under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), include all of the following in a single email:
dmca.intro: TextStack Reader respects copyright. If you believe your work has been copied and made available on this site in a way that infringes your copyright, use the process below to request removal.
dmca.misuseBody: Under Section 512(f) of the DMCA, anyone who knowingly materially misrepresents that material is infringing (or was removed by mistake) may be liable for damages. Please submit notices in good faith.
dmca.processBody1: Once we receive a valid notice, we will act expeditiously to remove or disable access to the material and notify the uploader.
dmca.processBody2: We typically respond within a few business days. Complex claims may take longer.
dmca.repeatBody: We terminate accounts of users who repeatedly upload infringing material.
dmca.req1: A description of the copyrighted work you claim has been infringed.
dmca.req2: The exact URL(s) on this site where the allegedly infringing material is located.
dmca.req3: Your full legal name, mailing address, phone number, and email address.
dmca.req4: A statement that you have a good-faith belief the disputed use is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
dmca.req5: A statement, under penalty of perjury, that the information in the notice is accurate and that you are the owner or authorized to act on behalf of the owner.
dmca.sendBody: Send the complete notice to our designated agent at
dmca.sendNote: Incomplete notices will not be processed. We may share your notice (including contact details) with the user who uploaded the disputed content.

home.faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
home.faq.isFree.a: Yes. The full catalog, reader, contextual explanations, translation, SRS flashcards, text-to-speech, and reading statistics are completely free. No credit card required, no hidden limits.
home.faq.languages.a: You can translate English text into 18+ languages including Spanish, French, German, Ukrainian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Portuguese, and more. The interface is available in English and Ukrainian.
home.faq.mobileApp.a: Yes. The Android app is on Google Play: same books and saved words, and it reads offline. There is no iOS app yet; on an iPhone, TextStack works in the browser.
home.faq.installAndroid.a: On your Android phone, open Google Play, search for TextStack and tap Install. The "Android app" link at the bottom of this page opens the same listing. Sign in with your account to see your books and saved words.
home.faq.installAndroid.q: How do I install the Android app?
home.faq.connectAssistant.a: Open "AI assistants" at the bottom of this page and sign in. Create a key and paste it into your assistant once, following the steps on that page. The assistant can then read the books you upload and save conclusions back to them. You can revoke the key at any time.
home.faq.connectAssistant.q: How do I connect my AI assistant?
home.faq.deleteAccount.a: Sign in, open the user menu in the top-right corner and choose "Edit profile". In the "Danger zone" section select "Delete account" and type DELETE to confirm. In the Android app, open the Profile tab and choose "Delete account". Deletion is immediate and cannot be undone.
home.faq.deleteAccount.q: How do I delete my account?
home.faq.offline.a: Yes. Download books for offline reading. Your progress, bookmarks, and vocabulary sync automatically when you reconnect.
home.faq.srsCards.a: When you save a word, it becomes an SRS flashcard. The system uses 5 stages — from Recognition to Mastered — spacing reviews so you remember long-term. Smart distractors make each review meaningful.
home.faq.srsCards.q: How do the SRS flashcards work?
home.faq.subheading: Everything you need to know about TextStack.
home.faq.tapTranslate.a: While reading, simply tap or click any word. You will instantly see the translation in your native language and can hear the pronunciation. No switching apps or copying text.
home.faq.techBooks.a: The catalog ships with thousands of public-domain classics. MIT/Apache/CC-BY licensed programming books are being added — priority given to Rust, Go, and systems titles. You can also upload your own EPUB or PDF at any time and read it with the full toolkit.
home.faq.techBooks.q: Do you have programming or tech books?
home.faq.uploadBooks.a: Absolutely. Upload EPUB or PDF files and read them with the full TextStack toolkit — translation, flashcards, TTS, and progress tracking.
home.faq.uploadBooks.q: Can I upload my own books?
home.faq.vsFriends.a: TextStack combines the reading experience of Kindle with the language-learning tools of LingQ — and it is free. Tap-to-translate, SRS flashcards, built-in text-to-speech, offline reading, and detailed statistics, all in one clean reader.
home.faq.vsFriends.q: How is TextStack different from Kindle or LingQ?
home.faq.whatIs.a: TextStack is a reader for people who want to finish the book they keep quitting — dense tech books and papers, or classic literature. Every word you tap gets a contextual explanation tied to the book's domain. Save words to a capped weekly SRS queue. Works on web and mobile, online or offline.

privacy.aiBody1: Most are optional: if you do not use the tutor, Explain or translation, those features send nothing. Uploading a book is the exception — it always sends the title, author and the opening of the first chapter to OpenAI, as described above.
privacy.aiBody2: AI output can be wrong. Explanations, translations and answers about a book are generated by a language model and should not be relied on as fact.
privacy.aiBody3: We do not train models on your content, and under OpenAI's API terms neither do they. We do keep records of AI requests, as described above, for quality and cost monitoring.
privacy.aiBody4: If an AI response is offensive or harmful, please report it using the contact address at the bottom of this page.
privacy.changesBody: If this policy changes materially we will update the date at the top, and for significant changes we will say so in the app or on the site. The October 2026 revision adds what earlier versions left out: the guest account the mobile app creates, what an upload sends to OpenAI and Open Library, mobile crash reporting, app updates, backups and log retention. The November 2026 revision adds that a guest account holding saved data is deleted after 90 days without use.
privacy.childrenBody: TextStack is not directed to children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect their personal information. If you believe a child has created an account, contact us and we will remove it.
privacy.collectBody1: Account. Your email address, display name, and a profile picture if you set one. If you sign in with Google or Apple we receive your email, name, profile image URL and a provider identifier. If you use a password, we store a cryptographic hash of it and never the password itself. A guest account has only a random identifier and a made-up placeholder address.
privacy.collectBody2: Content you create or upload. The books you upload — both the original file and the text extracted from it — plus your highlights, notes, bookmarks, saved vocabulary and collections. Uploaded books are private to your account.
privacy.collectBody3: Reading activity. Reading sessions (duration, words read, position), progress, goals, streaks and achievements. This is stored on our servers and linked to your account — guest or registered — which is what lets it sync across your devices. We use it to run the app, not for analytics.
privacy.collectBody4: AI interaction data. We keep records of AI requests: every tutor and upload-enrichment request, and a sample of translation and Explain requests. A record holds the text that was sent — the passage of the book, your question — and the model's answer. These request records are not linked to your account; email addresses and phone numbers are removed from them, but the passage and question are kept as sent. The tutor is the exception: its sessions, and the record of how it planned them, are saved with your account. We use these records to investigate quality problems and to monitor what the service costs to run.
privacy.collectBody5: Technical data. IP address, server request logs, rate-limiting counters, and device and operating-system type. Our web server's access logs record the IP address and the address of each page or API call, but not the part after the "?", which is where the text you send to be read aloud and the words you search for travel. Its error log can record a request in full, including that part, when the request is rejected or fails — for example when a rate limit is hit or the service is restarting. On the website only, analytics events if you accept analytics cookies.
privacy.collectBody6: Kept only on your device. Theme, fonts, reader layout preferences, and the offline copies of any books you download.
privacy.collectBody7: From the mobile app. If the app crashes or an error occurs, a crash report goes to Sentry: the error, the app version, the device model and operating system, a random installation identifier and a sample of performance timings. It carries no name or email, and the text of your requests is removed from it. When the app checks for updates it sends Expo a random installation identifier, the app version and the platform.
privacy.contactBody: Questions about this policy, or a request about your data? Reach out at
privacy.cookiesBody1: Essential storage keeps you signed in and remembers your reader preferences. It cannot be switched off without breaking the service.
privacy.cookiesBody2: The website asks for your consent before loading Google Analytics and Ahrefs Analytics. Analytics stays off until you accept, and you can decline. We use no advertising cookies, and the mobile apps ship no analytics or advertising SDKs at all.
privacy.intro: This policy explains what TextStack collects, why, who we send it to, and how long we keep it. It covers the textstack.app website and the TextStack mobile apps.
privacy.purposeBody: To run the reading service and sync your library across devices; to produce AI answers, explanations, translations, speech and book details when you ask for them or upload a book; to fix crashes; to prevent abuse and enforce rate limits; and to monitor reliability and what the service costs to operate.
privacy.retentionBody1: Account data and the content you create are kept until you delete them, or until you delete your account. A guest account that has been inactive for 30 days and holds nothing you saved — no books, library, progress, highlights, notes, bookmarks or vocabulary — is deleted automatically. A guest account that holds saved data is deleted, with its books and files, after 90 days without use; this rule took effect on 24 November 2026, so the 90 days count from that date at the earliest. Registering keeps everything.
privacy.retentionBody2: Cached translations, explanations and generated speech are deleted after 30 days. Our web server's access and error logs are deleted after 14 days. Application logs are capped by size and overwritten as new entries arrive, typically within days to a few weeks. Crash and error reports are kept for Sentry's retention period.
privacy.retentionBody3: AI request records are kept indefinitely — they are the operational record of what the service did and what it cost. They are not linked to your account, but they can contain the text that was sent. Tutor records saved with your account lose that link, or are deleted, when you delete the account.
privacy.retentionBody4: Backups. We back up the database and stored files every night: two recent copies on our server and encrypted off-site copies at Cloudflare, kept for up to about three months. Data you delete stays in those backups until they expire.
privacy.rightsBody1: You can access and export your data, correct it, or delete it. Deleting your account takes effect immediately and cannot be undone: the account, uploaded books, highlights, notes, vocabulary, reading history and stored files are removed in a single transaction. Copies in backups, caches, logs and crash reports expire on the schedule above.
privacy.rightsBody2: In the app: open the Profile tab, scroll to Delete account (or Delete guest data, for a guest account), and confirm. On the website: sign in, open the user menu, choose Edit profile, then use the Danger zone. You can also start a deletion request without signing in from the page below.
privacy.rightsHeading: Your rights, and how to use them
privacy.scopeBody1: TextStack is a reading platform. This policy covers the textstack.app website and the TextStack apps for Android and iOS.
privacy.scopeBody2: You can browse the public library without an account. On the website, reading without an account keeps your progress on your device until you upload a book or save a few words. In the mobile app, opening a book or the upload screen creates a guest account on our servers straight away, so your progress, highlights and vocabulary are stored there from the start, without a name or email.
privacy.scopeHeading: Who we are and what this covers
privacy.securityBody: Data travels over HTTPS and is stored on servers we control. Books you upload are private to your account. Backups are encrypted before they leave our server. Access to production systems is limited to the operator.
privacy.seoDesc: What TextStack collects, who receives it, and how long we keep it — including the AI features.
privacy.thirdPartiesAnalytics: Google Analytics and Ahrefs Analytics. On the textstack.app website only, and only after you accept analytics cookies. The mobile apps contain no analytics.
privacy.thirdPartiesAuth: Google and Apple. Only if you choose to sign in with them, and only to verify who you are.
privacy.thirdPartiesCloudflare: Cloudflare. Carries all traffic to the service as our DNS and network provider, and stores our encrypted off-site backups.
privacy.thirdPartiesEmail: Resend. Receives your email address in order to deliver transactional email such as a password reset.
privacy.thirdPartiesIntro: We do not sell your personal information and we do not share it with advertisers or data brokers. We do send data to the providers below, each only as far as a feature you used requires.
privacy.thirdPartiesOllama: Some AI work stays with us. The hints and multiple-choice options in vocabulary review are generated by a model running on our own servers and are not sent to anyone.
privacy.thirdPartiesConnectors: Assistants you connect yourself. If you connect TextStack to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another assistant, that assistant can read the books, highlights, notes and vocabulary you give it access to, and write notes and words back. You start this connection and can revoke it; what the assistant does with the data is covered by its own privacy policy.
privacy.thirdPartiesOpenai: OpenAI. Receives book text in four cases: when you use translation, Explain or the tutor (gpt-4.1-mini) — your question and the relevant passage — and, automatically, every time you upload a book: its title, author and the opening of its first chapter (a few hundred characters) are sent to fill in missing details such as genre, year and description. Under OpenAI's API terms this content is not used to train their models.
privacy.thirdPartiesSentry: Sentry. Receives error and performance data from our servers and from the mobile app when something fails, as described above. Server reports can include details of the failing request. Sentry keeps them for its own retention period.
privacy.thirdPartiesExpo: Expo. Delivers updates to the mobile app; receives an installation identifier, the app version and the platform each time the app checks for one.
privacy.thirdPartiesTts: Microsoft. Text you ask to be read aloud — a passage, a word, a saved sentence — is sent to Microsoft's Edge text-to-speech service to be turned into audio. We use the same public service the Edge browser uses for reading aloud; we have no separate agreement with Microsoft.
privacy.thirdPartiesOpenLibrary: Open Library (Internet Archive). When you upload a book, we look up its title and author in Open Library's public catalogue to fill in missing details. Only the title and author are sent.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.transfersBody: Several of the providers above — OpenAI, Microsoft, Open Library, Google, Apple, Resend, Sentry, Expo and Cloudflare — process data in the United States and elsewhere. Using the features that depend on them transfers your data there.

terms.acceptanceBody: By accessing or using TextStack Reader, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service. If you disagree with any part of these terms, you may not access the service.
terms.aiBody1: TextStack includes features powered by large language models: the tutor, Explain, and translation. Their output is generated, not verified, and can be wrong, incomplete or misleading. Do not rely on it as fact, and do not rely on it for advice of any kind.
terms.aiBody2: Using these features sends the text you selected or asked about, together with the surrounding passage, to our AI providers. See the Privacy Policy for who receives it and what is stored. If a response is offensive or harmful, report it to the contact address below and we will look into it.
terms.changesBody: We may update these terms from time to time. Significant changes will be communicated through the website. Your continued use of TextStack Reader after changes constitutes acceptance of the new terms.
terms.contactBody: Questions about these terms? Reach out at
terms.contentBody1: TextStack Reader provides access to public domain literature — works whose copyright has expired and that belong to the public. These books are free to read, share, and enjoy.
terms.contentBody2: Users may upload their own books to their personal library. You are responsible for ensuring you have the right to upload and access any content you add to the platform.
terms.disclaimerBody1: TextStack Reader is provided "as is" and "as available" without warranties of any kind, whether express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. While we strive to maintain accurate texts and reliable service, we cannot guarantee uninterrupted access or error-free content.
terms.disclaimerBody2: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, TextStack Reader is not liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or any loss of profits, data, or goodwill, arising from your use of the service.
terms.intro: By using TextStack — the textstack.app website or the TextStack mobile apps — you agree to these terms. They are meant to be fair and readable.
terms.ipBody1: The public domain books in our library are free for anyone to use. However, the TextStack Reader platform, design, and original content are protected by copyright.
terms.ipBody2: We credit sources where applicable and strive to provide accurate information about each work's origin and status.
terms.liabilityCap: Our total aggregate liability to you for all claims arising from or relating to the service is limited to the amount you have paid us in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. For users who have paid nothing, this amount is zero. Some jurisdictions do not allow certain limitations, so parts of this section may not apply to you.

mcp.connect.heading: Connect keys
mcp.connect.lead: Create a key, paste it into Claude or ChatGPT once, and it can read the books you upload and write conclusions back. The key does not expire; revoke it here whenever you like.
mcp.connect.signInLead: Sign in to create a key. It is tied to your account — that is what lets an assistant reach your library and nobody else's.
mcp.connect.guestLead: Create a free account to connect an assistant. A key reaches your library from outside the app, so it belongs to an account you can sign back into.
mcp.connect.shownOnce: Copy this now — it is shown once and cannot be recovered. We store only a hash of it.
connect.title: Connect an assistant
connect.lead: Create a key and paste it into Claude or ChatGPT once. It can then read the books you upload and write conclusions back into them. The key does not expire — revoke it here whenever you like.
connect.shownOnce: Copy this now — it is shown once and cannot be recovered. We store only a hash of it.
connect.chatgptHow: In ChatGPT, add a custom connector (it needs Developer mode), paste this URL, and choose “No authentication”.
connect.chatgptWarning: This URL is a password: anyone who has it can read and write your library. Don't share it. Lost or leaked? Revoke the key below and create a new one.
connect.configLabel: Claude Desktop config, with your key already in it
connect.signIn.title: Sign in to connect an assistant
connect.signIn.subtitle: Your assistant reaches your whole library until you disconnect it, so connecting needs an account rather than a guest session.
connect.oneStep.heading: Connect in one step
connect.oneStep.lead: Paste this address into your assistant, sign in to TextStack and allow. No key to copy.
connect.oneStep.claudeHow: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste the URL → Allow
connect.oneStep.chatgptHow: Plugins → Add → Create MCP App → paste the URL → Connect → Allow
connect.apps.heading: Connected apps
connect.apps.loadFailed: Could not load your connected apps.
connect.developers.heading: For developers
connect.developers.lead: Cursor, Claude Code, scripts — anything that takes a key instead of signing in. Keys you already made keep working.
chapterReview.connect.title: Connect Claude or ChatGPT in a minute
chapterReview.connect.lead: TextStack works inside your own Claude or ChatGPT — connect it once, it takes a minute. Paste this address, sign in and allow:
